process_area.title: Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application

value_stream.name: Trade Accounts Receivable Factoring, Invoice Discounting & Receivables Securitization

workflows.name: Eligible Invoice Batch Selection, Pooling & Submission to Factor

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-batch eligible invoices and submit straight-through to the factor.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
- operational: double-financing fraud detection with duplicate-submission guard (invoice-level uniqueness check).
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ineligible-submission risk**: submitting ineligible invoices causes funder rejection, fees, and covenant impact; mitigated by automated eligibility-gating.
- **Double-financing risk**: an invoice submitted twice (to two factors) is fraud; mitigated by a single assigned-status flag in AR preventing re-submission.
System Touchpoints: - Factoring eligibility/submission engine; AR (VS-16); concentration/limit check (W5395).

steps.activity: Select eligible invoices per criteria (W5395): approved customer, within age, undisputed, within concentration.
Pool into a submission batch with required data (customer, invoice, amount, terms, due date).
Gate eligibility automatically (W5395); exclude ineligible (over-age, disputed, over-limit).
Submit the batch to the factor via the factoring platform (W5398); obtain acceptance.
Record submission and update invoice status to "submitted/assigned" in AR (VS-16).

fields.Trigger: Factor accepts and funds a submission (W5401)

workflows.name: Factor Funding/Drawdown, Advance Posting & Bank Reconciliation

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-post the advance from the bank feed and reconcile to the accepted submission.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
- operational: daily bank/posting reconciliation with month-end close tie-out.
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury/cash), VS-17 (GL), VS-157 (revenue/sale accounting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Funding-discrepancy risk**: an advance short of the expected amount (fees, reserve, rejection) mis-states cash and receivables; mitigated by per-drawdown reconciliation.
- **Mis-posting risk**: posting the advance to the wrong GL account distorts the financials and derecognition; mitigated by defined GL mapping (W5397).
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/funding (VS-18); GL posting (VS-17); factoring accounting (W5397); bank reconciliation (CTL-19).

steps.activity: Receive the factor advance (advance rate × eligible batch) net of fees/reserve to BuildRight's account.
Post the advance to cash and the receivables-sale/factoring GL accounts (VS-17/VS-157/W5397).
Reconcile the advance to the accepted submission and facility terms (rate, advance, reserve).
Update facility utilization and available headroom (W5394).
Investigate and resolve any funding discrepancy with the factor.

fields.Frequency: Per notified customer/segment; per remit change

workflows.name: Customer Invoice Reissuance/Re-assignment & Remit-To Instruction Update

Automation Opportunity: - Remit-to auto-updated on assignment with customer-notification template.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (AR), VS-29 (master data), VS-107 (accounts), VS-14 (comms)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-directed-payment risk**: a customer paying the old remit-to (BuildRight) instead of the factor causes mis-application and reconciliation breaks; mitigated by clear customer communication and remit-to controls.
- **Stale-remit risk**: an un-updated remit-to on a customer record causes ongoing mis-direction; mitigated by assignment-status flags and verification.
System Touchpoints: - Customer master remit-to (VS-29); AR reassignment (VS-16); lockbox (W5398); communication (VS-14/VS-107).

steps.activity: For notification factoring: update the customer master remit-to to the factor/lockbox (W5396).
Reissue/re-assign invoices (where required) with the new remit-to and assignment notice.
Communicate the change to the customer (Trade Account Mgmt) to avoid mis-directed payment (W5404).
Update AR (VS-16) and customer master (VS-29) with the assignment/remit status.
Verify the customer's next payment routes correctly to the factor/lockbox.

fields.Trigger: Customer payment to the factor/lockbox (notification) or BuildRight (silent)

workflows.name: Lockbox/Cash Receipt Processing, Customer Payment Matching & Clearing

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-matching of lockbox remittance to assigned invoices; auto-routing.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
- operational: bank/lockbox reconciliation with remittance-to-invoice matching.
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (AR/cash application), VS-18 (treasury), VS-80 (payments)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unapplied-cash risk**: unmatched payments distort AR and the factoring reconciliation; mitigated by remittance-detail matching and daily reconciliation.
- **Float/routing risk**: collected funds not routed per the facility create exposure; mitigated by defined routing and reconciliation.
System Touchpoints: - Lockbox/factor remittance feed; AR cash application (VS-16); treasury routing (VS-18); bank reconciliation.

steps.activity: Receive lockbox/factor remittance data with customer/invoice references.
Match payments to the assigned invoices in AR (VS-16); clear the receivable and the factoring advance.
Route the collected funds per the facility (to the factor / to BuildRight net of advance).
Investigate and resolve unapplied/short/over-payments and unidentified remittances.
Reconcile the lockbox/factor account daily (CTL-19).

fields.Frequency: Event-driven (~1–5% of submitted invoices become dispute/short-pay/credit events)
fields.Participants: Factor/Funder, Trade Credit Insurer (VS-68), AR, Customer
fields.Trigger: Customer dispute, short-pay, or credit risk event on a factored invoice

workflows.name: Non-Recourse Credit Risk Event, Customer Dispute & Short-Pay Handling

Automation Opportunity: - Event-driven claim workflows with insurance-window alerts.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
- operational: credit-insurance claim validity checks; dispute-fraud review; dilution-rate accuracy in reserve true-ups.
Cross-references: - links to VS-68 (trade credit/insurance), VS-26 (insurance), VS-16 (AR/disputes), VS-125 (fraud)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uninsured-loss risk**: a non-recourse claim filed late (past the insurance window) is denied, leaving BuildRight/ factor exposed; mitigated by prompt claim filing within policy windows.
- **Recourse-buildup risk**: recourse events accumulating signal portfolio deterioration and future buybacks; mitigated by dilution analytics and reserve review (W5399).
System Touchpoints: - Credit-risk module (VS-68); trade-credit insurance claims (VS-68/VS-26); AR dispute (VS-16); dilution analytics.

steps.activity: Identify the event: dispute, short-pay, or customer credit deterioration on a factored invoice.
For non-recourse: file a claim with the trade-credit insurer (VS-68) within the policy window.
For recourse: prepare for buyback at recourse-period expiry (W5407) or negotiate cure with the customer.
Resolve the dispute/short-pay with the customer (links VS-16 dispute management).
Update dilution analytics and reserve/holdback (W5399/W5406).

fields.Trigger: Customer payment/close of factored invoice; periodic reserve settlement

workflows.name: Dilution Reconciliation, Reserve Release & Holdback Settlement

Automation Opportunity: - Reserve auto-released on invoice close net of computed dilution.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
- operational: dilution/reserve accuracy; CTL-31 (adequate reserve); CTL-30 (close).
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reserve-dispute risk**: disagreement with the factor on dilution/reserve release causes cash delay; mitigated by transparent dilution reconciliation and terms.
- **Mis-posting risk**: incorrect reserve-release posting distorts the financials; mitigated by defined GL mapping.
System Touchpoints: - Factoring reserve/holdback module; GL (VS-17); dilution analytics (VS-68).

steps.activity: On invoice payment/close, reconcile actual vs. expected (full vs. short-pay/dispute).
Compute dilution (short-pay/dispute as % of invoice) and impact on the reserve/holdback (W5399).
Release the reserve/holdback to BuildRight net of dilution per the facility terms.
Post reserve release/holdback settlement to GL (VS-17).
Report dilution vs. facility threshold to the funder and credit committee (W5410).

fields.Trigger: Recourse period expiry on an unpaid factored invoice (recourse factoring)
fields.Volume: ~400–1,250 buybacks/yr (~1–3% of the ~42,000/yr recourse-factored invoice book per W5401/W5406)

workflows.name: Recourse Period Expiry, Unpaid-Invoice Buyback & Repurchase Processing

Automation Opportunity: - Recourse-expiry auto-triggers buyback and re-recognition workflows.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
- operational: buyback accuracy; CTL-31 (adequate recourse reserve/provision); CTL-29 (consolidated reporting).
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (AR/collections), VS-68 (credit), VS-157 (re-recognize), VS-17 (GL)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Recourse-buildup risk**: high recourse activity signals the sale is in substance a borrowing (re-characterization) and erodes the working-capital benefit; mitigated by substance monitoring (W5415).
- **Loss risk**: bought-back invoices that never collect become losses; mitigated by provisioning (W5412) and collection effort.
System Touchpoints: - Factoring recourse engine; AR re-recognize (VS-16/VS-157); GL/provisioning (VS-17); collections (VS-16/VS-68).

steps.activity: Identify invoices unpaid past the recourse period (recourse factoring).
Repurchase/buyback the unpaid invoice from the factor per the recourse agreement (W5394).
Re-establish the receivable on BuildRight's books (re-recognize under PFRS 9 — W5397) and pursue collection (VS-16/VS-68).
Apply the recourse reserve/holdback (W5399) and provision for likely loss (W5412).
Monitor recourse activity for substance/re-characterization signals (W5397/W5415).

fields.Trigger: Securitization instrument selected (W5393); periodic investor reporting

workflows.name: Securitization Pool Reporting, Investor/Trustee Reporting & Servicing

Automation Opportunity: - Pool-performance auto-aggregated and investor reports auto-generated per the PSA.
Controls: - CTL-798 (ensure controlled execution — Invoice Sale, Factoring Drawdown, Notification & Cash Application (PA-189.2).)
- operational: pool-reporting accuracy; CTL-19 (cash/waterfall reconciliation); CTL-29 (consolidated/off-BS reporting).
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury/waterfall), VS-17 (GL), VS-100 (legal/SPV), VS-173 (investor/capital-markets disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Covenant/trigger-breach risk**: breaching a pool trigger (delinquency, excess spread) accelerates amortization/penalties; mitigated by trigger monitoring and early action.
- **Reporting-error risk**: inaccurate investor/trustee reports breach the PSA and expose to investor claims; mitigated by reconciled reporting and review.
System Touchpoints: - Securitization pool/servicing module; investor/trustee reporting; treasury/waterfall (VS-18); GL (VS-17).

steps.activity: Aggregate pool performance: collections, dilution, delinquencies, and credit events (W5405).
Prepare investor/trustee reports per the pooling-and-servicing agreement (covenants, triggers, waterfalls).
Reconcile pool cash flows and remit per the waterfall (senior fees, interest, principal, residual).
Manage pool covenants/triggers (e.g. excess spread, delinquency triggers) and report breaches.
Coordinate with the trustee/SPV and legal on pool administration (VS-100).
